questions: If the flattened list is empty (e.g., all sublists are empty or L itself is empty), what should happen? Should it raise an error, return an empty Axes, or plot a histogram with zero bins?
Are duplicate values across sublists counted only once per occurrence (i.e., histogram of raw flattened data) or is the histogram of unique values (frequency of each distinct integer)?
Should the histogram use density=True (normalized to probability) or density=False (counts)?
Is the order of sublists relevant for any processing, or only the combined flattened list matters?
What should be the title, x-label, and y-label of the Axes? Should they be set to specific strings or left default?
If a sublist contains only integers but is empty ([]), should it be silently skipped (as reference does) or raise an error?
Should the function close or show the plot, or is the caller responsible for managing the figure?
